Article 21
(1) The Regional Government is obligated to provide complaint services and provision of special service rooms at police offices, in the context of providing protection for women and children from acts of violence.
(2) The Regional Government and the community or social service institutions may establish recovery houses or safe houses.
(3) Further provisions regarding complaint services and social services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Sixth Part
Services for Victims of Acts of Violence

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the Regency of Hulu Sungai Utara.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the regional government administration of Hulu Sungai Utara Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Hulu Sungai Utara.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution of Hulu Sungai Utara Regency.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
6. Woman is a person of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
7. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
8. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of acts of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center.
9. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim.
10. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
11. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
Perda Kab. HSU Tahun 2016 Nomor 3 ttg Perlindungan Perempuan dan Anak
12. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
13. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
14. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or Regional Government apparatus or by individuals.
15. Service is action that must be immediately taken to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
16. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.
17. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of violence victims.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of acts of violence to their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
19. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.
20. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection.
21. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of Regional Government, and/or Non-Governmental Organization (LSM) that conducts assistance.
22. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a functional work unit positioned at the sub-district and regency level to organize integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of acts of violence in the context of empowerment of women and children victims of acts of violence.
23. Family Information and Consultation Center (PIK) is an institution positioned at the village/sub-district level that provides consultation services and social guidance to individuals, family members, communities facing disruptions to their social functions.
Perda Kab. HSU Tahun 2016 Nomor 3 ttg Perlindungan Perempuan dan Anak
24. Implementing officers or functional officers are health workers, psychologists, psychiatrists, social workers, legal aid workers who come from civil servants within their respective offices or special personnel employed at P2TP2A and PIK Keluarga.
25. Special Service Room, hereinafter abbreviated as RPK is a safe and comfortable room specifically designated for witnesses and/or victims of criminal acts including suspects of criminal acts consisting of women and children who deserve to be treated or require special treatment, and whose cases are being handled at the Police office.
26. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related offices, vertical agencies, and the community in carrying out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence.
27. Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
28. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
29. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children.
30. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on), who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.
31. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.

Part Five
Principles of Service and Assistance

Article 19
Letter a What is meant by "quick" is immediate action taken without complications or simplified procedures. What is meant by "safe" is a guarantee of service protection that feels comfortable, undisturbed, and served in a friendly manner, with respect and appreciation.
What is meant by "empathy" is an act of appreciating, respecting, caring, being friendly, and making happy which aims to please and calm the victim's heart.
Letter b What is meant by "guarantee of confidentiality" is an effort to guarantee certainty for victims that their identity, medical treatment and legal handling will not be disseminated.
Letter c What is meant by "easily accessible" is the provision of services and assistance for all people without regard to their social status, so that such services are affordable for those who are unable or relatively sufficient for those who are able.
Letter d What is meant by "no fees charged" is that the activities of providing services and assistance carried out by P2TP2A are not charged to victims.

Second Part
Form and Mechanism of Service

REGARDING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL
The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb and damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security. This is philosophically stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire Indonesian nation and the Indonesian homeland.
Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), it is obligated to fulfill these provisions. Human Rights state that, the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government.
Through Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent human rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation.
To fulfill the Right to life, children need food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. Protection from violence that threatens their safety and health must be provided from an early age. Protection is needed to prevent physical, mental and sexual violence and exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, education that is appropriate to their physical and psychological development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents are obligated to understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is needed for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled on defending the best interest of the child is needed to realize protection that is legal in nature.
Furthermore, it is not uncommon to find cases of women and children who experience problems of physical, psychological, sexual and social violence. For example, women and children who are victims of persecution, neglect, eviction and abuse by parents or other people. For women and children who experience these problems, the government must provide a Safe House (children protection home) or Integrated Service Center (PPT) for women and children victims of acts of Perda Kab. HSU Year 2016 Number 3 regarding Protection of Women and Children violence. The Safe House or PPT is a safe place and is friendly in nature for women and children. The PPT is equipped with companions from educators, doctors, psychologists, religious scholars/clergy and is networked with lawyers for women and children as well as the RPK Unit at the Police.
The fate of women and children victims of acts of violence must be given attention by the government. The large number of cases of acts of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low levels of economy, education, environments that are in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of acts of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.
For empowerment of victims of acts of violence, the Regional Government can establish an Integrated Service Center as a service center in the context of empowering women victims of acts of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of women and children victims of acts of violence.
From the framework above, the Regional Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children. From these various efforts, a legal framework will be realized in the implementation of protection for women and children.

Article 4
Letter a What is meant by "obtaining protection" is obtaining protection from individuals, groups and institutions both government and non-government.
Letter b What is meant by "obtaining information" is access and information about the existence of complaint centers, P2TP2A, and all matters related to the fulfillment of their rights and involvement in the decision-making process related to assistance and case developments.
Letter c What is meant by "optimal service" is service that includes medical, extensive medicolegal, psychosocial and legal.
Letter d What is meant by "continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage" is handling that does not stop at physical and psychological healing, but until the victim can resume life in society including the restoration of their good name.
Letter e What is meant by "confidential handling" is an effort to guarantee certainty for victims that their identity, medical treatment and legal handling will not be disseminated.
Letter f What is meant by "obtaining psychological assistance" is assistance provided by psychologists to victims suffering from trauma/other mental problems to restore the victim's mental condition. Whereas, legal assistance is assistance provided by persons and/or legal aid institutions to victims at every level of examination and throughout the legal process.
Letter g What is meant by "guarantee of rights related to the victim's status" is an effort to provide certainty and protection for victims as members of the family and society.

3.8.rationale: The original Indonesian text does indicate involvement of religious/spiritual counselling personnel within the integrated service context. In the PENJELASAN (General section) it states that the Safe House / Pusat Pelayanan Terpadu (PPT) is “dilengkapi dengan pendamping dari unsur pendidik, dokter, psikolog, ulama/rohaniawan …” (equipped with companions including religious scholars/clergy). This supports that spiritual/religious counselling/support is part of the service/assistance resources. This exact evidence was present in the retrieved English candidates ([3.8-51] mentions “religious scholars/clergy”). The judge was overly strict by requiring an explicit phrase “religious/spiritual counseling service unit,” even though the policy clearly includes ulama/rohaniawan as part of the companion/support team.

5.2.evaluator_rationale: None of the provided passages explicitly mention collaboration/engagement with religious organizations or religious leaders; references to 'mental and spiritual' matters or 'religious scholars/clergy' do not establish stakeholder collaboration.

5.2.rationale: In the original Indonesian regulation, there is no explicit provision about stakeholder engagement/collaboration with religious organizations or religious leaders as stakeholders. The only religious reference is in the explanatory section describing that the PPT/Safe House is equipped with companions including “ulama/rohaniawan” (religious scholars/clergy), which indicates availability of religious/spiritual support personnel, not formal engagement/partnership with religious institutions/leaders. The operative articles on cooperation/partnership (e.g., Pasal 24 on cooperation with government/province/other regions/universities/non-government; Pasal 25 on partnership with business) do not mention religious bodies. Therefore the judge’s “No” is consistent with the Indonesian text for an indicator framed as ‘religious engagement’ (stakeholder collaboration), and the golden “Yes” likely over-interprets the presence of clergy as engagement.

23. Family Information and Consultation Center (PIK) is an institution positioned at the village/sub-district level that provides consultation services and social guidance to individuals, family members, communities facing disruptions to their social functions.
Perda Kab. HSU Tahun 2016 Nomor 3 ttg Perlindungan Perempuan dan Anak
24. Implementing officers or functional officers are health workers, psychologists, psychiatrists, social workers, legal aid workers who come from civil servants within their respective offices or special personnel employed at P2TP2A and PIK Keluarga.
25. Special Service Room, hereinafter abbreviated as RPK is a safe and comfortable room specifically designated for witnesses and/or victims of criminal acts including suspects of criminal acts consisting of women and children who deserve to be treated or require special treatment, and whose cases are being handled at the Police office.
26. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related offices, vertical agencies, and the community in carrying out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence.
27. Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
28. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
29. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children.
30. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on), who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.
31. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.

Seventh Part
Empowerment of Victims of Acts of Violence

CHAPTER XIII
SANCTION PROVISIONS
Article 34
(1) Every person who intentionally does not provide protection to women and children resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows violence to occur and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in the applicable laws and regulations.
(2) If Officials appointed to provide protection do not carry out their obligations and responsibilities, they shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.
Perda Kab. HSU Tahun 2016 Nomor 3 ttg Perlindungan Perempuan dan Anak (3) Managers of P2TP2A Regency/District and PIK Keluarga Village/Sub-district who carry out service duties that violate service principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the internal mechanisms of P2TP2A and PIK Keluarga.

Article 8
(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 6 letter b, shall be implemented in the form of community participation.
(2) The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or the authorized party; and
c. participating in providing assistance and/or handling of victims of acts of violence.
(3) The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 2
Letter a What is meant by "respect for the rights of victims" is a series of actions to respect, appreciate and ensure the fulfillment of the rights of victims.
Letter b What is meant by "justice and gender equality" is a process to be fair to men and women and equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, defense and National security activities and equality in enjoying the results of such development.
Letter c What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.
Letter d What is meant by "the best interests of victims" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, must be the primary consideration.
Perda Kab. HSU Year 2016 Number 3 regarding Protection of Women and Children

Article 3
Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear.
Paragraph (2) Letter a What is meant by the "prevention" aspect is a protection strategy effort through:
a. primary prevention, all people, families, communities and the state in efforts to increase the ability of knowledge, understanding and ensuring that violence against women and children does not occur, including policy socialization, adequate services, supportive workplace policies, and life skill training for women and children. What is meant by life skill training includes conflict resolution without violence, stress management skills, resource management, making effective decisions, effective interpersonal communication, guidance on the psychosocial development of women and children.
b. secondary prevention, aimed at community groups with high risk in efforts to increase skills, including training and victim services to ensure that violence against women and children does not occur in the next generation. Activities carried out here include conducting home visits for parents who have just had children to conduct self assessment whether they are at risk of committing violence against children in the future.
c. tertiary prevention, intended to increase parenting abilities that ensure that violence against women and children is not repeated, here what is done is integrated services for women and children who are victims of violence, through counseling, stress management training.
Letter b What is meant by the "service and assistance" aspect is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals and assistants in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
Letter c What is meant by the "reunification" aspect is an effort to restore and recover the physical and psychological condition of victims which then reunites them with the victim's family and community.
Letter d What is meant by the "empowerment" aspect is a process of increasing the role of the community to participate in the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence which aims to obtain access and participation in the process of protection of women and children broadly.
Perda Kab. HSU Year 2016 Number 3 regarding Protection of Women and Children

6.8.rationale: The original Indonesian text does involve the legal process and law-enforcement handling mechanisms. Pasal 21(1) requires complaint services and “penyediaan ruang pelayanan khusus di kantor kepolisian” (special service rooms at police offices). The regulation also includes BAB XII PENYIDIKAN (Pasal 33) authorizing PPNS to conduct investigations, including receiving reports/complaints, summoning witnesses/suspects, seizures, and coordinating with police/prosecutors. These are clear legal-process-related provisions. The judge’s “Yes” based on Article 21 is directionally correct (and even stronger support exists in Pasal 33), so the golden label “No” appears incorrect for an indicator about legal process involvement.
